profile.behavior: Moves deliberately along branches, gleaning insects and spiders from foliage, bark, and twigs; also makes short flights to catch airborne insects. Usually forages from eye level into the canopy and may join mixed-species flocks outside the breeding season.
field_marks: White cheeks bordered by a black mustache stripe
Black streaking across the back and flanks
Two bold white wing bars on long, pointed wings
Small, thin, pointed bill and dark eye
Orange-yellow legs and a short tail
profile.habitat: Breeds chiefly in boreal spruce and tamarack forest, young evergreen stands, and alder or willow thickets. During migration it uses scrub, evergreen forest, and deciduous woodland; in winter it occupies forest edges, second-growth woodland, and wooded canopy.

findings: The primary specimen is a convincing breeding male Blackpoll Warbler matching the attached references: black cap, white cheeks bordered by a dark mustache stripe, streaked back and flanks, two white wing bars, dark eye, thin pointed bill, orange-yellow legs, long pointed wings, and a relatively short tail.

The plate contains exactly one complete primary specimen with one head, one beak, one tail, two anatomically coherent legs and grasping feet, and a convincing wing pair with the far-side wing naturally occluded.

The detached wing and head are clearly intentional supplementary studies rather than duplicate parts attached to the primary bird. Both studies are anatomically coherent; the head study has a complete eye and consistent bill proportions.

The common name, scientific name, family, measurements, habitat, behavior, and all six field-mark lines are legible and match the proposed text without visible omissions, substitutions, duplications, or nonsensical wording.
Cornell directly supports the displayed compatible measurement set for both sexes: 14 cm (5.5 in) length, 12–13 g (0.4–0.5 oz) weight, and 21–23 cm (8.3–9.1 in) wingspan.

Cornell and Audubon independently support the depicted breeding-male identity and major field marks, including the black cap, white cheeks, streaked sides or flanks, white wing bars, pointed wings, and yellowish or orange-yellow legs.

The body-length schematic has the required 0 cm (0 in) bottom endpoint and 14 cm (5.5 in) top endpoint, increases from bottom to top, agrees with the published length, and retains “SCHEMATIC — NOT TO SCALE.”
